mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and depresses S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS falls > 2% over 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing output and economic momentum, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when INDPRO rises > 0.5% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points and a decline in average hourly earnings (HOUST) below -0.2% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND HOUST falls > -0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when both UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and HOUST falls > -0.2% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25 percentage points signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below -5% signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which reduces economic growth and depresses S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when HOUST falls > 5% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 5% signals a deepening economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings and depresses S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS falls > 5% over 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).
